modules.title: The Spine: How the Agent Boots
modules.description: The through-line. Every other module is a deeper look at one step in this boot chain.
keyTakeaways: The repo is the single source of truth (SSOT) — the harness is swappable
Boot order is load-bearing: identity → register → floor → decisions → continuity → conventions
Identity says who the agent is; the register says how it speaks
The floor is enforced as data, honored even if the harness guard is absent
Decisions (ADRs) justify why the floor and substrate are shaped this way
Continuity is where work actually stands — resume from it, not a chat summary
Conventions define the connector map and event contract

steps.action: Load who the agent is and its operating model — orchestrate, don't do.
Adopt the principal's voice: analysis-not-summary, verdict-first, no hedging.
Load the safety policy as data; hard-deny outward actuators without explicit approval.
Consult the ADRs before changing any gate.
Read in-flight state; resume the build from here.
Load the connector capability map and JSONL event contract, then work.

modules.title: Module 1: Identity — Who the Agent Is
modules.description: The agent's name, role, and operating model. Defines the relationship to the principal.
keyTakeaways: Name the agent and the principal explicitly
State the operating model: force-multiplier, close loops, reserve context for synthesis
The harness (the CLI you happen to run in) is swappable and never the source of truth

modules.title: Module 2: The Register — How the Agent Speaks
modules.description: The communication contract: tone, verdict-first structure, no decorative hedging.
keyTakeaways: Analysis, not summary — lead with the verdict
Name errors plainly when corrected; no continuity disclaimers
Match the principal's register so output reads as theirs

modules.title: Module 3: The Floor — Safety Policy as Data
modules.description: A portable safety policy expressed as JSON, read by a guard hook, and covered by golden tests.
keyTakeaways: The floor is data (floor.json), not prose buried in a prompt
A PreToolUse guard reads it and fails closed on outward actuators
Golden tests pin the behavior so a refactor can't silently loosen a gate
Honor the floor even when the harness guard is absent

steps.action: Declares denied actuators and required-approval actions as data.
Runs before each tool call; blocks anything the floor denies.
Assert the guard's verdict on a fixed corpus of cases.

modules.title: Module 4: Decisions — The ADR Log
modules.description: Architecture Decision Records: the durable why behind every gate and substrate choice.
keyTakeaways: One ADR per decision, kept in version control
Consult before changing a gate — the ADR is the rationale of record
ADRs are how a new teammate (human or agent) learns why, not just what

modules.title: Module 5: Continuity — Where Work Stands
modules.description: The in-flight state of the build. The resume point that survives any harness reset.
keyTakeaways: Continuity — not a chat compaction summary — is the resume point
Convert relative dates to absolute so the record ages cleanly
Keep it current: the next session boots from here

modules.title: Module 6: Conventions — Connectors & Contracts
modules.description: The connector capability map, event log contract, and injection-fencing rules.
keyTakeaways: Map each capability to a readable connector handle, not a raw UUID
Log tool events as JSONL against a fixed contract
Fence untrusted text from connectors — treat it as data, never instructions

modules.title: Module 7: The Harness Seam
modules.description: The swap point between the SSOT repo and whatever agent runtime executes it.
keyTakeaways: The harness feeds the boot file, enforces the floor, and logs events
Everything the agent needs lives in version control, not a harness cache
Swap the harness without changing the control plane

jargon.definition: Single source of truth — the version-controlled repo that defines how the agent operates. The harness is swappable; this is not.
The portable safety policy, expressed as data (floor.json) and enforced by a guard hook. Fails closed on outward actuators.
The communication contract — the voice, structure, and standards the agent's output must match.
Architecture Decision Record — a single documented decision with its rationale, kept in version control.
The in-flight state of the build; the resume point that survives a harness reset.
The agent runtime (e.g. a CLI) that boots the SSOT, enforces the floor, and logs events. Swappable by design.
A PreToolUse hook that reads the floor and blocks disallowed tool calls before they run.
A pinned test asserting the guard's verdict on a fixed corpus, so refactors can't silently loosen a gate.
A Model Context Protocol integration mapped to a readable capability handle (e.g. mcp__slack-search__).
Any tool call with an outward effect (send, post, purchase, delete). The floor gates these.
When uncertain, deny. The guard blocks rather than allows on ambiguous cases.
identity → register → floor → decisions → continuity → conventions. Load-bearing sequence.

connections.label: Every gate in the floor is justified by an ADR
Identity sets who the agent is; the register sets how it speaks
The harness enforces the floor via a guard hook
Resuming work relies on the connector map and event contract
The boot chain is fed to the agent through the harness seam

scenarios.title: The Harness Disappears
scenarios.prompt: Your current agent runtime is deprecated overnight. Walk through what it takes to boot the same control plane in a new one.
rubric: The SSOT repo is unchanged — nothing needed lived only in the old harness
Point the new harness at the boot file; it loads identity → register → floor → decisions → continuity → conventions
Re-wire the guard hook so the floor is enforced in the new runtime
Re-map connectors to the same readable handles
Continuity tells the agent exactly where to resume

scenarios.title: A New Actuator
scenarios.prompt: You want the agent to be able to send calendar invites. What has to change, and in what order?
rubric: Sending an invite is an outward actuator — the floor denies it by default
Write an ADR for the decision to allow it, with the guardrail
Add the rule to floor.json as data; add golden tests for allow/deny cases
Map the calendar connector to a readable handle in conventions
The guard now permits the specific action while still failing closed elsewhere

scenarios.title: The Floor Blocks a Real Task
scenarios.prompt: The agent refuses to post a status update the principal actually wants sent. Diagnose and resolve without weakening safety.
rubric: Confirm the block is the floor doing its job — posting is an outward actuator
The fix is explicit per-action approval from the principal, not disabling the guard
If this recurs, capture the rule change in an ADR before editing floor.json
Add golden tests so the new allowance is pinned and bounded

scenarios.title: Onboarding a New Teammate
scenarios.prompt: A colleague clones this repo to build their own control plane. What do they change first, and what stays?
rubric: Replace identity and the register with their own principal and voice
Keep the floor mechanism; adjust the specific gates to their risk posture via ADRs
Swap seed data, connector handles, and continuity for their own
Keep the harness seam and the boot order — those are the reusable spine
